title: P0 hosted API multiplex fairness collapse — field diary and runbook draft
content:
Summary:

This doc captures the immediate timeline, impact, mitigations, hypotheses, and a first-pass runbook for the P0 incident on 2029-07-16 where hosted API streaming and multiplexed connections experienced a fairness collapse that cascaded into TTFB/streaming latency spikes and elevated 5xx rates across a subset of tenants. The root cause is an interaction between the new multiplex scheduler fairness heuristic (mux-fair-v2) and adaptive batching/eviction heuristics that produced pathological shard starvation and KV-cache churn.

Impact:
- Start: 2029-07-16 02:18:42 UTC — anomaly detection alerted on TTFB p95 for hosted-api-prod in us-west1.
- Peak impact window: 02:26 — 03:12 UTC.
- Symptoms: p95 TTFB rose from ~210ms to 3.8s for streaming endpoints; p99 increased to ~9.4s.
- Error surface: 5xx rate increased from baseline 0.2% to 7.6% for multiplexed routes (stream create/stream write).
- Customers: ~18 high-traffic tenants saw streaming reconnects and partial payload truncation. Several reported API-level timeouts and increased error budgets.
- Business: short-lived but customer-visible degradations; SLO burn for streaming routes estimated ~18% for the hour.

Immediate timeline (what happened, who did what):
- 02:18 UTC: Synthetic monitors and internal TTFB alerts fired. On-call (Aisha) acknowledged and started paging.
- 02:21 UTC: SRE triage channel collects traces; initial signal shows many sessions stuck in multiplex scheduler queue waiting >2s before being dispatched.
- 02:24 UTC: Diego pulled scheduler telemetry; observed a growing skew in per-tenant request assignment — a small fraction of shards monopolizing worker slots.
- 02:28 UTC: Ruth noted increased KV-cache eviction rates and miss spikes coincident with scheduler skew. Correlation: sessions hitting different workers caused cache thrash and longer fetch times to backing store.
- 02:33 UTC: Temporary mitigation attempted: increase multiplex worker pool size by +25% (scales out allocator). Small improvement but latency still high.
- 02:41 UTC: Emergency rollback of mux-fair-v2 feature flag to mux-fair-v1 (last known-good) started.
- 02:49 UTC: After rollback, TTFB p95 began trending down; by 03:06 UTC p95 back to ~260ms. 5xx rate normalized by 03:12 UTC.
- 03:20 UTC: Incident declared mitigated; on-call moved to post-incident analysis.

What we changed during the incident (mitigations, fixes):
- Emergency rollback of mux-fair-v2 (feature flag).
- Short-term: scaled mux worker pool to absorb backlog (+25% ephemeral capacity), increased stream-create rate-limiter on edge for multiplexed clients to prevent repeated reconnects.
- Telemetry: turned on additional per-shard fairness metrics and KV-cache eviction histograms for the rest of the recovery window.

Root cause hypothesis (triage findings):
- Primary cause: the newer fairness heuristic (mux-fair-v2) attempted to equalize scheduling across logical tenants by moving short sessions to underutilized shards; combined with adaptive batching/v3 it produced churn where small bursts of traffic were repeatedly rebalanced between different workers.
- Secondary cause: the rebalancing amplified KV-cache fragmentation (prefix caches are per-worker) which raised cache miss rates and caused backend lookups (metadata store) to spike. That increased request service time, which fed back into the fairness controller and further rebalanced load — positive feedback loop.
- Amplifier: slightly increased client churn (some clients with aggressive reconnect logic) made the scheduler see many short-lived sessions which mux-fair-v2 prioritized, worsening thrash.
- Not a cause: underlying network fabric and GPU serving were healthy; no node-level resource starvation (CPU, memory, NIC) detected.

Evidence and signals:
- Telemetry: per-shard dispatch latency CDF showed a bimodal distribution as queues grew on a subset of shards.
- KV-cache metrics: eviction rate jumped 6x, miss latency to metadata store rose from median 2ms to ~24ms during peak.
- Logs: scheduler emitted per-tenant rebalance logs with unexpectedly high frequency (rebalance cycles per minute went from ~2 to ~48).
- Linked artifacts: see Slack thread https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01234567/p1689590400000000 and JIRA-SRV-4123 for initial incident worklog.

Why this wasn't caught in staging:
- Staging load generator did not simulate the high-churn short-session pattern seen in production tenant mix. The fairness heuristic was validated under steady-state shaper traffic only.
- KV-cache load tests were run with larger working sets that hid small-fragment thrash scenarios.

Immediate lessons learned (short bullets):
- Scheduler fairness changes need chaos tests that include short-session churn and aggressive reconnect patterns.
- Per-worker cache coherence/hotspot metrics must be part of any fairness rollout gating.
- Feature flags for scheduling heuristics must have an automated slow rollout with telemetry-based abort triggers.

Runbook draft (first-pass automated + human steps) — for similar future incidents:
1) Alert triage
   - If streaming TTFB p95 > 1.5s AND 5xx rate for streaming routes > 1% for 5m, set P0.
2) Rapid containment (SRE on-call)
   - Check scheduler fairness flag state: is mux-fair-v2 enabled? If yes, flip to previous stable (mux-fair-v1) and monitor for 5m. Owner: on-call.
   - Increase multiplex worker pool by +20% if backlog > 10s across shards. Owner: infra-scaling runbook.
   - Enable stream create slow-path rate limiter at edge (throttle reconnect storms) — edge SLO knob doc (link placeholder).
3) Diagnostic steps (parallel)
   - Pull per-shard dispatch latency and rebalance-cycle rate.
   - Check KV-cache eviction rates and backing-store latency.
   - Capture live trace of a few affected sessions (span: scheduler -> worker -> kv-store).
4) If rollback not possible quickly:
   - Apply targeted patch to fairness: pause inter-shard migration for sessions < 3s. (This reduces churn.)
5) Post-mitigation validation
   - Wait 15 minutes after changes; validate p95/p99 and 5xx trending down for 30 minutes before declaring mitigated.

Longer-term action items (owners and deadlines):
- MUX-89: Add integration tests for short-session churn scenarios to mux-scheduler CI (owner: Diego Morales, ETA: 2029-08-06).
- SERV-2567: Add per-worker cache coherence telemetry and gating for scheduling rollouts (owner: Ruth Chen, ETA: 2029-08-13).
- SRE-4123: Automate feature flag slow-roll with telemetry abort (on metric signal: rebalance-rate > 10/min or kv-evictions > 3x baseline) (owner: Aisha Patel, ETA: 2029-07-30).
- PERF-773: Review adaptive-batching-v3 parameter space to ensure it doesn't oscillate with fairness (owner: Lina Park, ETA: 2029-08-20).
- Docs: Update runbook and add checklist for controlled rollouts of scheduling heuristics (owner: Omar Haddad, ETA: 2029-07-25).

Open questions / unknowns to follow up in postmortem deep-dive:
- Could we have detected the positive feedback earlier with an anomaly detector on rebalance cycle rate? (Answer: likely yes; add to SRE-4123.)
- Exact threshold where cache fragmentation causes backend latency amplification — need targeted microbenchmarks.
- Any clients whose reconnect behavior violates best practices and amplified issue? Create SRE-4124 to contact top 5 tenants and review client patterns.

Post-incident retrospective notes (tone + human):
- What went well: quick rollback path via feature flags; on-call composure, clear Slack triage; targeted scale-up bought us time to rollback safely.
- What could be better: our canary traffic didn't mimic production churn; dashboards lacked a single correlated metric that would have indicated the rebalance-thrash pattern earlier.
- Communication: need a small customer note template for short P0s that hit streaming (owner: product-comms).

Appendix: quick checklist for next on-call shift
- Verify mux fairness flag automation exists in ops-console and that abort thresholds are configured.
- Add per-shard rebalance-rate to the default SRE dashboard.
- Smoke test streaming endpoints after any fairness rollout for 30 minutes with churn generator job (job id: churn-smoke-13).

Notes to self (Aisha):
- Keep this field diary style — other incidents were missing the rapid mitigation chronology.
- Follow up with Diego on test harness changes; ask Lina for batching experiments she promised.
- Schedule 1-hour postmortem deep-dive with eng-serving-runtime / mux scheduler / platform infra next Tue 2029-07-23. Calendar invite: internal.

END OF DRAFT
